scope: The splitting method generalizes Part 1 to handle integrals with both lower and upper limits variable, by decomposing into integrals with constant lower limits.
warrant: The method uses Part 1 on each split integral after reversing limits, thus extending the theorem to more complex integration limits.

rationale: The relation claims that the splitting method generalizes Part 1 to handle integrals with both limits variable. The premise (Part 1) states: if f is continuous on [a,b] and F(x)=∫_a^x f(t) dt, then F'(x)=f(x). The conclusion (splitting method) states: to differentiate an integral with both limits variable, split at a constant point, reverse the lower-limit integral with a sign change, and apply the Fundamental Theorem and chain rule. The evidence passages (p75–p81) show exactly this: F(x)=∫_x^{2x} t^3 dt is split into −∫_0^x t^3 dt + ∫_0^{2x} t^3 dt, then differentiated using Part 1 (d/dx[−∫_0^x t^3 dt] = −x^3) and chain rule (d/dx[∫_0^{2x} t^3 dt] = (2x)^3·2 = 16x^3), yielding F'(x)=15x^3. The scope, warrant, and all substantive assertions are directly grounded in the supplied evidence. The relation is supported.
